Bubblehead here, USN, and red lights are used when a sub is going to PD or surfacing at night or at any other time it is deemed necessary. The purpose of red light is this: The human eye is "least sensitive to red light for night vision". So we go from white to red to allow all eyes in control to adjust their vision for night vision. As far as this idea where it will shoot white light out the periscope? That can happen, but you needed your eye on the scope to have great night vision.

When a boat surfaces, regardless of time of day, there is an officer's eyeball glued to it who constantly walks in circles to look for anything we might run into or come up under. Both of which have happened.

Now this is talking about old school technology. Newer tech? Nope, nothing from inside can get out since the periscope has no glass: Photonics Mast. These newer periscopes do not penetrate the hull, so there is no chance of a periscope failure or damage to allow seawater in. It also allows the Control Room to be positioned anywhere they need to because the new Photonics Mast is completely electronic and outside the pressure hull.

What hasn't changed is that to go to into the sail for any reason headed topside you still travel from the control room to the sail, so Rig for Red is still a thing, and it is just for night vision.
